source: The 11 Google Doc almanacs linked with the collection text (icons included, embedded in the docs).
note:
Import record for the 11 characters of The Bazaar, written from the Google Doc almanacs the owner linked beside the collection text. Everything is the authors' own: flavour line, ability, summary, examples and how-to-run all come from those docs, and nothing was written that they do not say. Notes:
- The icons came out of the docs themselves. Each almanac embeds its icon as a base64 PNG (1080x1080), so no separate icon set was needed; they go through the site's own 591x591 resize, the same transform as assets/art-normalize.js.
- The Worrywart doc has no image at all - its own JSON block lists "image": "..." as a placeholder - so that page is saved as a DRAFT. A character with no icon cannot be published (assets/classify.js, PUBLISH_REQUIREMENTS), and the Worker would refuse it anyway. Everything else about the page is complete and it will publish the moment art exists.
- The Worrywart doc also states its ability twice and differently: the almanac line reads "Public and private announcements might be false, even if dead." and its JSON block reads "Storyteller announcements might be fake.". The almanac line is stored, since that is the one the other ten docs use for their abilities too.
- Two of the names already belong to other creators here: Bilge Rat (the High Seas of Mutiny Traveller) and Gargoyle. Those two take a -the-bazaar URL in the wiki's existing duplicate style; the other nine keep their plain slug. This Bilge Rat is a Minion and unrelated to the pirate one.
- The docs carry no night order, no reminder tokens and no setup flags, so those fields are empty. They are almanac pages, not a script.json.
- Credit is "Patters, Alex S.", matching the collection, whose own text says "Character Creation by Patters & Alex S". The docs do not credit individual characters, so nothing finer was invented. The comma makes each name its own creator page, and Alex S. matches the spelling already used by Fall of Rome.
- appearsIn is "The Bazaar", which the collection's match[] ("thebazaar") picks up, so the roster filled itself. The collection carries Starlight, and a Starlight collection lends the status to its members, so all ten published pages read as Starlight rather than Partial even though the set has no tags.
- Written straight to D1, so settings.content_version was bumped by hand after the write.

characters.name: Fly
characters.ability: You secretly join the game. All players learn this when you first vote.
characters.lede: The Fly joins the game without being announced.
summaryBullets: The Fly is a player in the game like any other, they sit in a particular place, must keep their eyes closed at night and learns the Demon if they are evil.
The Storyteller should only acknowledge the Fly as being in-play once they have voted.
The first time the Fly votes, their vote is counted and after the vote the Storyteller announces that they have joined the game.
The Fly should indicate to the Storyteller that they’d like to join the game as covertly as possible.
howToRun: Each day, if the Fly votes on any nomination, count their vote and at the end of the vote announce that they are the Fly.
examples: Alex turns up an hour late to the start of the game. Upon their arrival, they nod to the Storyteller who understands the signal. The next night, the Storyteller wakes Alex to tell them they are good. The next day, they vote on the first nomination and they are announced as the Fly.

Tom has to leave to catch the train in an hour. Tom says he will “sit this game out”, but truthfully the Storyteller and he both know he will travel as the Fly. During the night, the Storyteller wakes Tom and tells him he is evil and who the Demon is. Tom never votes and is never announced as the Fly.
characters.creator: Patters, Alex S.

characters.name: Bilge Rat
characters.ability: Outsiders poison Townsfolk they nominate until dawn. [Exactly 3 Outsiders]
characters.lede: The Bilge Rat makes Outsiders poison Townsfolk.
summaryBullets: When Outsiders nominate Townsfolk, the Townsfolk become poisoned.
The poison effect happens immediately and lasts until dawn.
If the Bilge Rat is in play, there must be exactly 3 Outsiders during setup.
The Bilge Rat’s Outsider modification trumps all other Outsider setup effects.
If the Bilge Rat enters mid-game, the setup part of their ability has no effect.
howToRun: While setting up the game, before putting the character tokens in the bag, remove as many Townsfolk or Outsiders as needed to ensure there are exactly 3 Outsiders in-play. Replace any Outsiders you remove with Townsfolk, and any Townsfolk you remove with Outsiders.
Each day, if any Outsiders make a nomination and the player they nominate is a Townsfolk, mark the Townsfolk player with the POISONED reminder token.
Each dawn, remove all POISONED reminder tokens from players.
examples: The Sloth nominates the Nightwatchman. The next night, the Nightwatchman chooses to use their ability, but it has no effect.
The Politician nominates the Artist. After the nomination, the Artist asks a question and gets a wrong answer because they are now poisoned.
The Hatter nominates the Godfather. The Godfather is unaffected because they are not a Townsfolk.
characters.creator: Patters, Alex S.

characters.name: Sloth
characters.ability: If you are the only good player alive, you become evil.
characters.lede: The Sloth becomes evil if they’re the only good.
summaryBullets: The Sloth only becomes evil if there are no other good players alive.
The Sloth changes alignment immediately after the condition is met.
A drunk or poisoned Sloth cannot become evil.
howToRun: Each night, check if the Sloth is the only alive good player. If they are, wake them. Show the YOU ARE info token then give a thumbs down. Put them to sleep. Turn their character token upside down. (This shows they are now evil.).
examples: The Sloth is alive with a Farmer, Steward, Mastermind and No Dashii. The Farmer is executed and the Steward killed by the No Dashii during the night. The only alive good player is the Sloth, so they become evil.
characters.creator: Patters, Alex S.

characters.name: Skeptic
characters.ability: There is a non-listed character in-play. [1 evil player is that character]
characters.lede: The Skeptic brings non-listed characters in-play for the evil team.
summaryBullets: The Storyteller decides which non-listed character will be in-play during setup.
The non-listed character must be the same type of the evil player.
The Skeptic does not learn which non-listed character has been added into play.
If the non-listed character you have added has setup effects, apply those as well.
If the Skeptic enters mid-game, it has no effect.
howToRun: While setting up the game, decide which non-listed character in-play will be in-play, then remove a token that matches the character type of the non-listed character you chose. This non-listed character token goes into the bag instead of the listed character token. If the non-listed character token has any setup effects, also apply those now too.
examples: The Storyteller chooses that the Demon in this game will be the Ojo, even though it is not listed on the script.
The Storyteller chooses that one of the Minions in this game will be a Baron, even though it is not listed on the script. The Storyteller also removes 2 Townsfolk and adds 2 Outsiders during setup.

There is a Bounty Hunter in-play which means there is an evil Townsfolk in-play. The Storyteller chooses to put a Snake Charmer, even though it is not listed on the script. The Snake Charmer must be the evil Townsfolk in this game.
characters.quote: Oh, sure, it's all a nice, simple conspiracy! All your troubles are caused by a handful of people working in predictable ways! And pigs can fly!
characters.creator: Patters, Alex S.

characters.name: Gargoyle
characters.ability: If you died by execution this game, you may choose to die or be resurrected at any time.
characters.lede: The Gargoyle controls whether they’re alive or dead.
summaryBullets: The Gargoyle may choose to use their ability at any time day or night. It may also be done privately or publicly.
If the Gargoyle chooses to come back to life, or die during a vote - this does not affect the required majority.
The Gargoyle must die by execution to gain control over their lifecycle.
Dead players cannot die again, so if the Gargoyle is executed after they die this has no effect.
howToRun: During the day, if the Gargoyle dies by execution, mark the Gargoyle with the HAS ABILITY reminder.
Each night, if the Gargoyle is marked with the HAS ABILITY reminder, wake the Gargoyle. If they wish to live, they give a THUMBS UP signal and if they wish to die, they give a THUMBS DOWN signal.

If the Gargoyle chooses to live, they become alive again – mark them with the ALIVE reminder and remove their shroud. At dawn, after declaring which players died, declare which player is alive again. (Do not say why.) If the Gargoyle chooses to die, they die immediately – mark them with the DEAD reminder token and place a shroud on them. At dawn, declare they have died. (Do not say why.)

During the day, if the Gargoyle is marked with the HAS ABILITY reminder, the Gargoyle may visit you privately and state they wish to die or be resurrected – mark them with the relevant reminder tokens and make announcements as appropriate.

At any point during the game, if the Gargoyle is marked with the HAS ABILITY reminder, the Gargoyle may publicly announce whether they wish to die or be resurrected. If they do, mark them with relevant reminder tokens and make announcements as and when appropriate.
examples: The Gargoyle is executed on day 3, they choose to immediately come back to life.

The Gargoyle is executed on day 1, the Demon is about to be voted on so they come to life to increase the required majority by one, and then after the vote is concluded choose to die again, lowering the majority again.
The Gargoyle is killed during the night by the Alchemist with the Assassin’s ability. They cannot choose to come back to life.
characters.creator: Patters, Alex S.

characters.name: Midnight
characters.ability: Each night*, choose a player: they die. After good nominations exceed players, evil wins. All players learn when 3 remain.
characters.lede: The Midnight limits the number of nominations by good players.
summaryBullets: All players learn when good players can only make 3 more nominations.
They learn this after the nomination that triggered this has concluded.
Any number of nominations can be made, but if good players make too many nominations the evil team wins.
Travellers do not count towards the player count for the Midnight’s ability.
Calling for a cult & or nominating a Traveller for exile do not count towards Midnight's nomination count.
The Midnight’s nomination count is global, so Storytellers should keep count if it is possible for Midnight to enter play mid-game.
howToRun: Each night except the first, wake the Midnight. The Midnight points at any player. Put the Midnight to sleep. The chosen player dies - put the Midnight’s DEAD reminder token in the grimoire and place a death shroud on them.

During the day, after each nomination by a good player - decrease the Midnight’s nomination tracker by 1. If the number on the tracker reaches 3: announce to all players that there are only 3 nominations left.
If the number reaches the death icon on the tracker, the game is over and the evil team has won.
examples: There are 10 players in the game. On day 1, good players make 6 nominations on day 1. On day 2, a good player nominates and the Storyteller announces there are 3 nominations left. On day 3, 2 good players make nominations. On day 4, another 2 good players make nominations. The game ends, and the evil team wins.
characters.creator: Patters, Alex S.

characters.name: Bell-Ringer
characters.ability: If the number of living evils outnumbers the number of living goods, you are resurrected.
characters.lede: The Bell-Ringer warns good players when there are too many evils alive.
summaryBullets: If there are more evil players than good players alive, the Bell-Ringer comes back to life.
As long as they are healthy & sober, there is no limit to how many times they can do this.
If the Bell-Ringer is alive, they are not informed they would come back to life.
The Bell-Ringers ability only works whilst they are dead.
It does not matter how the Bell-Ringer dies as it is a continuous check.
If an execution or kill would cause 2 players to live, the game ends before the Bell-Ringer comes back to life.
howToRun: When the number of living evil players exceeds the number of alive good players, add a night token to the Bell-Ringer’s entry on the night sheet. Each night, if the Bell-Ringer has a night token on the night sheet, the Bell-Ringer becomes alive again – mark them with the ALIVE reminder and remove their shroud. At dawn, after declaring which players died, declare which player is alive again. (Do not say why.)
examples: There are 7 good players and 3 evil players. On night 4, 5 of the good players are dead, including the Bell-Ringer. The Bell-Ringer is resurrected.

There are 9 good players and 5 evil players. 3 evil players are dead and 7 good players (including the Bell-Ringer) are dead. On night 5, the evil players don’t outnumber the good players so the Bell-Ringer is not resurrected.
There are 7 good players and 3 evil players. On night 3, 5 of the good players are dead, but the Bell-Ringer is alive. The Bell-Ringer learns nothing.
characters.quote: One if by land... thirteen by midnight... though it cost ye yer lives, the town must know! Pull in the ropes lads and hang on the bell!
characters.creator: Patters, Alex S.

characters.name: Schai
characters.ability: On your 1st night, look at the Grimoire & choose all players. Each night*, the 1st chosen player who can die does so.
characters.lede: The Schai decides all their kills at the start of the game.
summaryBullets: On the first night, the Schai sees the Grimoire and decides who dies in what order.
On subsequent nights, they are not woken to choose who dies.
They must choose all players, including themselves.
Players who are safe from the Demon (or otherwise cannot die) are skipped when determining who dies.
howToRun: During the first night, wake the Schai and show them the Grimoire for as long as they need. Hand them a notepad & pen and have them write down all the players in the order they want them to die. Put the Schai to sleep.
Each night except the first, refer to the list that the Schai wrote and find the first player who can die tonight, that player dies – mark them with the “Dead” reminder.
examples: It is a 14 player game. On the first night, the Schai chooses the Monk, Fortune Teller, Poppy Grower, Drunk, Marionette, Gossip, Knight, Empath, Dreamer, Spy, Oracle, Shugenja, Scarlet Woman and Schai.

It is a 7 player game. On the first night, the Schai choose Empath, Noble, Innkeeper, Amnesiac, Alsaahir, Devil’s Advocate and Schai. On the second night, the Empath is protected by the Innkeeper so the kill goes to the next player who can die, the Noble.
characters.quote: Your fate is sealed and your death nears. Give in.
characters.creator: Patters, Alex S.

characters.name: Bandwagon
characters.ability: Once per game, during the day, publicly choose to become the alignment the Storyteller believes is winning.
characters.lede: The Bandwagon joins the winning team.
summaryBullets: The Bandwagon can choose to use their ability at any time during the day, and must declare to everyone when they're using it.
After declaring they want to use their ability, the Storyteller privately tells the Bandwagon the team they are now on.

The Storyteller is the judge on which team is winning. Many factors may be included, such as how many players of each team are still alive, how much information the good team has, how successful the evil team’s bluffs seem to be, which players the group wants to execute next, or how experienced the Demon player is. All of these, and more, will inform the Storyteller’s judgment.
Players may say whatever they want at any time, so a player who's pretending to be the Bandwagon may pretend to use the Bandwagon ability.
howToRun: During the day, the Bandwagon can declare that they wish to use their ability. If so, take the player aside, decide which team is currently winning and inform them of their new alignment. The Bandwagon loses their ability – put the NO ABILITY reminder token by the Bandwagon token.

If a player is bluffing as the Bandwagon and declares they wish to use their ability, act as if they were indeed the Bandwagon – take them aside, pretend to inform them of their alignment and act like you’re fiddling with reminder tokens.
examples: The only players who are dead are evil. The Bandwagon declares that they wish to join the winning team. The Storyteller takes them aside and informs them that they are still good.

There are 3 players alive and the Bandwagon nominates themselves and gets enough votes to be executed. Before they are executed, they declare that they wish to join the winning team. The Storyteller takes them aside and informs them that they are now evil.
characters.quote: Oh, I was always a fan of... What was it again? Demon worship?
characters.creator: Patters, Alex S.

characters.name: Emissary
characters.ability: You start knowing 1 of the Demon's bluffs & an in-play good character.
characters.lede: The Emissary learns a Demon bluff and an in-play character.
summaryBullets: On the first night, the Emissary learns 2 good characters: one of which is a Demon bluff and one of which is an in-play good character.
On subsequent nights, they learn nothing more.
The Emissary can learn any good character token: Townsfolk or Outsider.
howToRun: During the first night, wake the Emissary and show them one in-play good character token and one Demon bluff. Put the Emissary to sleep.
examples: Tom is the Shugenja and the Demon bluffs are Undertaker, General and Pixie. The Emissary learns the Undertaker and the Shugenja.

Alex is the Vortox and the Demon bluffs are Monk, Farmer and High Priestess. The Emissary learns Huntsman and Dreamer - neither of which are in-play. The Emissary must learn out-of-play characters that are not Demon bluffs because the Emissary’s information must be false due to the Vortox’s ability.
characters.quote: There is a corpse on the road. I could barely recognise them. No papers, no clothing, no face... I fear the worst.
characters.creator: Patters, Alex S.

characters.name: Worrywart
characters.ability: Public and private announcements might be false, even if dead.
characters.lede: The Worrywart makes players doubt the Storyteller.
summaryBullets: An announcement is something a player learns due to another players’ ability.
The Storyteller can choose to lie to players about things that they would normally learn.
The Storyteller may choose to lie at any point during the game.
The Storyteller cannot lie about players alignments and/or living status via this ability.
howToRun: At any point during the game, make an announcement that isn’t true.
examples: The Storyteller announces it is Day 1 of a Leviathan game. There is no Leviathan in-play.
The Storyteller tells the Steward & the Dreamer that the other person is the Evil Twin.
Neither player is the Evil Twin.
The Storyteller announces the Fearmonger has chosen a new target.
This is because they did. The Storyteller did not lie.
characters.quote: ...Yes. I have read “The Boy Who Cried Wolf”. Why do you ask?
characters.creator: Patters, Alex S.
